Recommended protocol, synthesized from the literature: freeze the trained model in evaluation mode; construct each target’s preceding history, truncate once to the original input window, then perturb only that window—never refill deleted positions from older history. Retain its final item when deleting or shuffling earlier interactions; separately test final-item removal. Match exact deletion counts across random, oldest-first and recent-first deletion, preserving survivor order. Reapply identical left padding and final-nonpadding readout. Include unchanged input and last-item-only input through the same checkpoint; this measures that model’s dependence on additional history, not the capability of a separately trained last-item model. Fix perturbation seeds, repeat random perturbations, and report paired changes with uncertainty. Shuffling can conflate behavioral order with item availability, limiting its interpretation. [Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/)

Cache identical candidate sets across conditions: one target plus 99 unique negatives, excluding the target and applying the benchmark’s original history exclusions before perturbation. Never let deletion change candidate eligibility. Rank deterministically by descending score, then item ID; avoid target-favoring ties. Preserve legitimate earlier occurrences of repeated target items, report repeat versus novel-target results separately, and identify duplicated diagnostic examples so they do not silently overweight outcomes. Candidate sampling can change model comparisons, so sampled HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog performance. [On Sampled Metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

When targets already participated in training, label results in-sample sensitivity diagnostics. Degradation indicates dependence on the supplied context under that intervention; it cannot distinguish useful memory from memorization, establish causal importance, or demonstrate future generalization. Synthetic deletions and permutations introduce distribution shifts. Generalization claims require untouched temporally held-out targets; preserve the host’s fixed evaluation separately. [Data Leakage in Offline Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060)
